+//! The waterjet profile operation's stored parameters (#1883): what the
+//! op keeps, as heights and plain numbers - resolved into the motion
+//! crate's `waterjet::WaterjetParams` at generation.
+//!
+//! Provenance: our own parameter set over general abrasive-waterjet
+//! practice (kerf side, leads with the pierce in the scrap, tabs as
+//! uncut gaps, pierce and abrasive dwell) and RS-274 / ISO 6983 for
+//! G41/G42 and linear-only controls. No torch height or THC field.
+
+use super::height::Height;
+
+/// Which side of an open run's travel the kerf stands on.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum JetSide {
+    #[default]
+    Center,
+    Left,
+    Right,
+}
+
+/// The shape of the leads.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum JetLead {
+    #[default]
+    Arc,
+    Straight,
+}
+
+/// Tabs left as uncut gaps: count, width (mm) and one position per tab
+/// (world X, Y), near a closed contour.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct JetTabsOp {
+    pub count: u32,
+    pub width: f64,
+    pub at: Vec<[f64; 2]>,
+}
+
+/// The waterjet profile's parameters.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct WaterjetOp {
+    /// The jet-off travel plane.
+    pub clearance_z: Height,
+    /// The sheet's top: the plane the cut rides.
+    pub top_z: Height,
+    /// The sheet's bottom: nothing steps down to it - a waterjet cut goes
+    /// through in one pass.
+    pub bottom_z: Height,
+    /// The kerf width override, mm; `None` reads the nozzle tool's
+    /// diameter (its kerf width).
+    pub kerf: Option<f64>,
+    /// Post G41/G42 for the control to offset, instead of the computer's
+    /// offset path.
+    pub control_comp: bool,
+    /// Outer contours counter-clockwise and holes clockwise.
+    pub reversed: bool,
+    pub lead: JetLead,
+    /// Lead-in / lead-out length, mm; 0 = none.
+    pub lead_in: f64,
+    pub lead_out: f64,
+    /// The kerf side of open runs.
+    pub open_side: JetSide,
+    /// `None` = no tabs.
+    pub tabs: Option<JetTabsOp>,
+    /// Cut feed, mm/min (the stated cut data).
+    pub feed: f64,
+    /// The pierce dwell and the abrasive's delay before it, s.
+    pub pierce_time: f64,
+    pub abrasive_delay: f64,
+    /// Arcs sent as chords within this tolerance, mm; `None` keeps them.
+    pub linearize: Option<f64>,
+}
+
+impl WaterjetOp {
+    /// Structural sanity (no world): every number finite and in range.
+    /// The motion crate's door repeats the refusals by name at
+    /// generation; this is the command door's yes / no.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn is_sane(&self) -> bool {
+        let nneg = |v: f64| v.is_finite() && v >= 0.0;
+        let pos = |v: f64| v.is_finite() && v > 0.0;
+        self.clearance_z.is_sane()
+            && self.top_z.is_sane()
+            && self.bottom_z.is_sane()
+            && self.kerf.is_none_or(pos)
+            && nneg(self.lead_in)
+            && nneg(self.lead_out)
+            && pos(self.feed)
+            && nneg(self.pierce_time)
+            && nneg(self.abrasive_delay)
+            && self.linearize.is_none_or(pos)
+            && self.tabs.as_ref().is_none_or(|t| {
+                t.count > 0
+                    && t.count as usize == t.at.len()
+                    && pos(t.width)
+                    && t.at.iter().all(|p| p[0].is_finite() && p[1].is_finite())
+            })
+    }
+}

+//! The waterjet profile's file mirror (#1883): the op's parameters as
+//! plain keys (blank options absent, no tabs absent). Additive - no
+//! older file names the kind, so absent keys never need a default.
+//! Provenance: our own file format (`project/mod.rs`); the names are ours.
+
+use super::*;
+
+use crate::operation::{JetLead, JetSide, JetTabsOp, WaterjetOp};
+
+#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
+pub enum JetLeadDto {
+    Arc,
+    Straight,
+}
+
+#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
+pub enum JetSideDto {
+    Center,
+    Left,
+    Right,
+}
+
+#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct JetTabsDto {
+    pub count: u32,
+    pub width: f64,
+    pub at: Vec<[f64; 2]>,
+}
+
+#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct WaterjetDto {
+    pub clearance_z: HeightDto,
+    pub top_z: HeightDto,
+    pub bottom_z: HeightDto,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub kerf: Option<f64>,
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub control_comp: bool,
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub reversed: bool,
+    pub lead: JetLeadDto,
+    pub lead_in: f64,
+    pub lead_out: f64,
+    pub open_side: JetSideDto,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub tabs: Option<JetTabsDto>,
+    pub feed: f64,
+    pub pierce_time: f64,
+    pub abrasive_delay: f64,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub linearize: Option<f64>,
+}
+
+impl WaterjetDto {
+    pub(super) fn from_op(p: &WaterjetOp) -> Self {
+        WaterjetDto {
+            clearance_z: p.clearance_z.into(),
+            top_z: p.top_z.into(),
+            bottom_z: p.bottom_z.into(),
+            kerf: p.kerf,
+            control_comp: p.control_comp,
+            reversed: p.reversed,
+            lead: match p.lead {
+                JetLead::Arc => JetLeadDto::Arc,
+                JetLead::Straight => JetLeadDto::Straight,
+            },
+            lead_in: p.lead_in,
+            lead_out: p.lead_out,
+            open_side: match p.open_side {
+                JetSide::Center => JetSideDto::Center,
+                JetSide::Left => JetSideDto::Left,
+                JetSide::Right => JetSideDto::Right,
+            },
+            tabs: p.tabs.as_ref().map(|t| JetTabsDto { count: t.count, width: t.width, at: t.at.clone() }),
+            feed: p.feed,
+            pierce_time: p.pierce_time,
+            abrasive_delay: p.abrasive_delay,
+            linearize: p.linearize,
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub(super) fn to_params(&self) -> OpParams {
+        OpParams::WaterjetProfile(WaterjetOp {
+            clearance_z: self.clearance_z.into(),
+            top_z: self.top_z.into(),
+            bottom_z: self.bottom_z.into(),
+            kerf: self.kerf,
+            control_comp: self.control_comp,
+            reversed: self.reversed,
+            lead: match self.lead {
+                JetLeadDto::Arc => JetLead::Arc,
+                JetLeadDto::Straight => JetLead::Straight,
+            },
+            lead_in: self.lead_in,
+            lead_out: self.lead_out,
+            open_side: match self.open_side {
+                JetSideDto::Center => JetSide::Center,
+                JetSideDto::Left => JetSide::Left,
+                JetSideDto::Right => JetSide::Right,
+            },
+            tabs: self.tabs.as_ref().map(|t| JetTabsOp { count: t.count, width: t.width, at: t.at.clone() }),
+            feed: self.feed,
+            pierce_time: self.pierce_time,
+            abrasive_delay: self.abrasive_delay,
+            linearize: self.linearize,
+        })
+    }
+}

+## #1883 - Waterjet Profile operation and the shared 2D sheet kernel
+
+**What was decided.**
+
+1. A new module `motion::sheet` holds the 2D sheet kernel. It contains:
+   - `nest` (contour roles and the inner-first cut order) and `ring`
+     (kerf ring and walks), moved from `plasma`;
+   - `laws` (the kerf law and the cover law) and `lead` (lit pieces,
+     straight and arc leads), moved from `plasma`;
+   - `arclen` (a ring by arc length), moved from `wire_edm::tabs`;
+   - `open` (the one-sided mitred offset of an open run), moved from
+     `wire_edm::open`.
+
+   Each refusal names its operation and tool through a `Voice`, so that
+   the plasma and wire EDM messages stay word for word. The plasma golden
+   CL and all plasma and wire EDM tests pass without a change.
+2. The cover law now takes one span or more for each contour (one for
+   each stretch between tabs), and an `exempt` closure for the edge
+   points that a tab leaves uncut on purpose. Plasma passes "no point is
+   exempt". The law now refuses a closed contour that has no span.
+3. `motion::waterjet::waterjet_profile` cuts as follows:
+   - inner contours first;
+   - the kerf ring at kerf / 2 on the waste side;
+   - straight or arc leads with the pierce in the scrap. A lead that has
+     no room is halved up to four times;
+   - the tight-hole rule. A hole whose lead has no room after the
+     halving is pierced at its centre and led in straight.
+   - tabs as uncut gaps. A tab is laid on the nearest closed contour.
+     Each stretch between gaps gets its own pierce and its own leads.
+   - open runs on the centre line, or on the left or right side.
+   - optional G41/G42, with the plasma's straight-entry rule;
+   - optional arc linearization through `Move::chords`.
+
+   The kerf and cover laws certify the result.
+4. `OpType::WaterjetProfile` uses the stored id 44 and
+   `Section::Waterjet` (`Family::Waterjet`). It mounts a `ToolKind::Waterjet`
+   nozzle only. `.camproj` stores it as `waterjet_profile` (additive).
+   MCP reaches it through the generic `add_operation` / `edit_operation`.
+5. The op stores its cut data as explicit numbers: cut feed, pierce time,
+   abrasive delay, and an optional kerf override (the nozzle's diameter
+   by default). The pierce time and the abrasive delay go into the path's
+   notes only. The CL record that carries them to the post is #1882.
+6. A tabbed contour, a centre-pierced hole and an open run use the
+   computer's offset under control compensation, and a note says so.
+   Each stretch between tabs is too short to be a safe G41/G42 span.
+
+**Why.** The maintainer asked for an end-to-end WAZER path (comment on
+#1883, 2026-11-20). The issue asks for the kernel to be shared "without
+duplicating geometry logic". Moving the code without a change, behind a
+voice parameter, keeps the plasma and wire output byte for byte (the
+goldens prove it). The waterjet then reuses the same certified laws.
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+
+- Reuse of `wire_edm::tabs::tabbed` for the waterjet tabs. The wire
+  threads once and retraces its kerf to each stretch, and it adds a tab
+  cut-off pass. A waterjet pierces each stretch. Only the arc-length ring
+  is common, and that ring is now shared (`sheet::arclen`).
+- A waterjet CL record (`WaterjetCut`, jet spans). That record is #1882's
+  scope. Until #1882 merges, the path carries notes only, and no post
+  serves `Kind::Waterjet`.
+- Selection of the cut data from the nozzle's recipe (`waterjet_row_for`
+  by stock material and sheet thickness). The generation job does not
+  carry the stock material, and `operation/job.rs` is changed by many
+  open PRs. This is a follow-up issue.
+- Refusal of control compensation together with tabs. Riding the
+  computer's offset with a note is safer and does not refuse a legal
+  program.
+
+**Cost to change later.** The stored id 44 and the `waterjet_profile`
+file key are permanent. An open PR that also appends a kind takes the
+next free id when it merges second. The cut data can move to the recipe
+without a file change: an absent field can mean "read the recipe".
